lines.speaker: harrow
lines.text: Keep your voice down, friend, and welcome to what's left of Oakhaven.

lines.speaker: harrow
lines.text: Gate's shut after dusk. Keep it low.

lines.speaker: harrow
lines.text: You shout like that again and I'll put you out through the thorn myself.

lines.speaker: lyra
lines.text: You came. Sit, keep your voice in your chest. I've a thing to ask that I should not ask anyone.

lines.when: !(flags.lyra_wg_met || flags.lyra_dw_met)   // from voices.js lyraState(): after Whisper-Grove she is silent until flags.lyra_voice, then speaks as lyra_ruined

lines.speaker: lyra
lines.text: Lower. Please. There are things in this town that learn from every sound.
lines.when: !(flags.lyra_wg_met || flags.lyra_dw_met)   // from voices.js lyraState(): after Whisper-Grove she is silent until flags.lyra_voice, then speaks as lyra_ruined

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Mind the bed, twenty paces off the door. No sound carries over it for a day. Say what you came to say.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: The hounds let you past. That means you came quietly. Good.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: I don't build things anymore. I just know how they break. What do you want broken?

lines.speaker: hetty
lines.text: Sit anywhere that isn't broken. Small beer or smaller. We do not sing in here, not since Davin.

lines.speaker: hetty
lines.text: Beer's a copper. Rooms are a sovereign. Singing is free and it will get you killed.

lines.speaker: hetty
lines.text: I've put bigger men than you out of here for raising their voice. Sit.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Every sailor dies, friend. The trick is to be somewhere else when it happens. Sit; I'm buying, because I'm frightened.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Corsair, Rust Coast, retired from the sea on account of the sea. What'll you have?

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Ha! You have the look of somebody about to tell me something I already know and have been drinking not to hear.

lines.speaker: rooke
lines.text: I have cut more limbs than any butcher in the Reach and done every one with care. Sit. I will not chalk your door today.

lines.speaker: rooke
lines.text: The sap-mark means past cutting. Now it also means the Inquisitor's list. Keep that to yourself.

lines.speaker: rooke
lines.text: Lower your voice in my surgery or I will lower it for you with a needle.

lines.speaker: orla
lines.text: Come closer, I cannot turn. Are you here about Davin?

lines.speaker: orla
lines.text: Mind the roots on the floor. They are mine.

lines.speaker: orla
lines.text: I am a tree with a tongue; shout at me if you like, I cannot leave.

lines.speaker: pim
lines.text: Shh. Mam says I'm not to talk to anybody about my hands.

lines.speaker: pim
lines.text: I'm not supposed to be out. Don't tell.

lines.speaker: vosk
lines.text: Pitch has a colour, through these lenses. Yours is an unremarkable brown. State your business.

lines.speaker: vosk
lines.text: The Consortium pays this town's bread. Remember that before you speak.

lines.speaker: vosk
lines.text: I have Legionnaires. You have a voice. One of those is replaceable.

lines.speaker: aldric
lines.text: The seal of Queen Maelis bids you welcome. Her signature on the decrees is famously steady for a woman dead a hundred and forty years.

lines.speaker: aldric
lines.text: Yes? Be brief. I have the Factor at one shoulder and the Church at the other.

lines.speaker: aldric
lines.text: You sold them, my son says. I fed them, I say. Which of us do you think is lying?

lines.speaker: tobiah
lines.text: Night shift. Keep it under the pumps and the bells won't turn. Are you — are you with him? With Engineer Vance?

lines.speaker: tobiah
lines.text: Nobody comes down here who isn't on the roster. Which you aren't.

lines.speaker: tobiah
lines.text: Quiet! The Legionnaire in Depot Three walks when it hears boots.

lines.speaker: bettany
lines.text: Softly, love. What ails? I have tonic, I have honey for the throat, and I have shot, which I do not approve of and sell anyway.

lines.speaker: bettany
lines.text: Tonic's five. Honey's four. Shot's three the three. Keep your voice down while you count.

lines.speaker: bettany
lines.text: I hummed half this town into the world. I will not be barked at in my own stall.

lines.speaker: tam
lines.text: Sit if you like. She comes on the water about this time. You will hear her if you keep still.

lines.speaker: tam
lines.text: Hm. You are standing where I listen.

lines.speaker: tam
lines.text: Lower your voice. She will not come if you shout.

lines.speaker: hob
lines.text: Evening. Mind the vats; the lime does not care who you are.

lines.speaker: hob
lines.text: Tannery's shut. Nobody wants leather off a town that is turning to wood.

lines.speaker: hob
lines.text: I have buried two apprentices this year. Try me.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: He is not to be looked at. Whoever you are. He has a cough.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: The mill is shut. Say what you want through the door next time.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Get out of my mill.

lines.speaker: ignatius
lines.text: The Note is held. You may speak under it. Quietly, and in tune.

lines.speaker: ignatius
lines.text: This chapel had bells once. The Synod took them for bore-teeth, and it was right to. A bell is a voice with nobody inside it.

lines.speaker: ignatius
lines.text: I have burned men for less than that tone. I am tired, and the Note is long, and you will not try me again.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.text: Evening. Keep it low.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.text: Hm?

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.text: Lower your voice before something hears you.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.text: Blessings of the Narrow on you. Softly, now.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.text: Yes? Quietly.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.text: Hush! The children.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Entry: a stranger, polite, at the wrong end of the continent. Sit. Not there. That is where the proctors will come from.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: I am a list, not a cure. Say what you came to say.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Precision, please. I record everything, including the tone.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Mind the ladder; the third rung is a liar. She'll hold at the mast-height as long as the tanks do, and the tanks are not what they were.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: OK-114, under two coats of paint. She's initialled it eleven times, your scribe. I can tell by the way she looks at my hull.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Say it quick. I don't like a city that doesn't fall down.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Listen. Under the water. Seven forty-one, very faint. The presses.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: This is a dead city that never fell down. That is a statistical anomaly. I do not like anomalies.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: My arm locks when that note is struck near it. Keep me away from the grey men, or keep them away from me.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Entry: the stranger is polite in a drowned city. Noted.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: I am a list, not a cure.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Precision, please. I record everything, including the tone.

lines.speaker: halder
lines.text: Four plates. The blue one is Bryony's.

lines.speaker: halder
lines.text: The boys will be in directly.

lines.speaker: halder
lines.text: Sit, sit, there's four.

lines.speaker: quist
lines.text: Hot water? There is always hot water. Sit; the chair is clean. People hesitate less when the chair is clean.

lines.speaker: quist
lines.text: You are not on my list, which means you are on someone else's. Sit down.

lines.speaker: quist
lines.text: Lower your voice. There are people being registered in the next room, and it upsets them.

lines.text: DEFEND THE SINGERS.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Ten heartbeats. I counted. This time I didn't cut.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: She's on her side in the willows with a hole in her number-three tank you could post a sheep through. We are not leaving by air today.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Don't. I know. I put a tree through an Office cutter. It seemed like the thing to do.

lines.speaker: tobiah
lines.text: Don't touch that. Or that. That one you can touch, it's already broken.

lines.speaker: tobiah
lines.text: Number-three tank. Look at it. I could weep. I nearly have.

lines.speaker: tobiah
lines.text: I'm an engine man in a forest. Say something useful or hold this.

lines.speaker: mags
lines.text: Slower. I read lips, not minds.
lines.delivery: flat, dry; the first word is an instruction, the second sentence a dry aside

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Seven forty-one is gone. I can hear the woods instead. They are very loud.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Not now.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Entry: the Deep Woods. One wreck, eleven souls, a press, and me.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Two things left in the inventory, and the third does not feel like a gap. It feels like a shelf.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: I am counting. Wait.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: DEFEND THE SINGERS.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: DEFEND THE SINGERS.

lines.text: One more before the light goes. One more.

lines.speaker: sexton
lines.text: Deep enough. Not deep enough. One more.

lines.text: Lilies for the Cantor. Lilies.

lines.speaker: mourner
lines.text: We're late. The bell hasn't gone.

lines.text: SHE IS GIVEN. THE QUIET IS MERCIFUL. GO.
segments: SHE IS GIVEN. THE QUIET IS MERCIFUL. GO.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: About time. I go where it's loudest and break what's about to break. You keep us in the Narrow.
lines.delivery: dry; the first words a wry greeting; a faint glass ring may sit under them
segments: I go where it's loudest and break what's about to break. You keep us in the Narrow.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Hear that? The tombs are holding a chord under the floor. Something in here is about to break, and it isn't the stone.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Old bronze. Cracked at the lip, on the east side. Ring it hard and it'll go the rest of the way.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Quiet. Glass won't ring inside one. Iron, and keep moving.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: A funeral office with nobody in it. My arm hates it.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Marble. Hit it where it's already cracked: the elbows.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Office. They hear better than they fight. Kill the horn first.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Static on legs. Cut the threads, not the spider.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: That one's full. I can hear them in her, waiting to hatch.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: They're not making a sound. Not breathing, not footfalls. That takes practice.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Crossbows. Close the distance, or get a willow between you and them.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Felted bell. Don't let it touch you before you've sung what you need.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Hounds. They won't touch the glass. Stay near me.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: You're bleeding into the moss. Back off and let me take it.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Wake me if the arm starts ringing. You'll hear it before I do.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: I'm fine. The arm's ringing, that's all. Give me a minute.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: I don't build things anymore. I just know how they break.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Every willow here has a split about a hand above the root. Damp gets in. Give it ten years.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: The glass is louder out here. Like standing next to a bore that's still turning.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: My father sold the Root to keep the town fed. I keep trying to hate him for it. I keep doing the arithmetic instead.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Lyra taught me the Root note when we were nine. I still hum it when the arm's bad. Don't tell her.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Hounds won't come near the glass. Neither will most people. It's restful.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: There. That's what it sounds like when something stops.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Structural failure. Finally.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Next.
lines.delivery: flat; follows the narration that he flexes the glass hand until it stops ringing

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: The House of the Veil. The scribes kept everyone's names in here. I never thought I'd walk on theirs.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: Nobody has rung for the dead out here in three years. You can hear it in the woods. They're waiting.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: That's the office for the dead, sung wrong. Every third line missing. It makes my teeth ache.
lines.delivery: low, warm; her own ruined voice

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: I can't sing near it. Nothing can. Don't let it get between us.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: They cut out their own tongues to be holy. I taught children whose parents did that.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: They're wearing voices. Little ones. Don't listen too closely.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: Hounds. Stay low. I'll keep us in the Narrow.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: It's listening for me. It has been listening for me since Oakhaven.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined

lines.delivery: low, warm; her own ruined voice

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: Hold still. I've got you.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: I'll take first watch. I'll hum. Sleep.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: I'm not built for this. I'm a teacher.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: I told my father once that a martyr is just a musician who gave up before the coda. He wrote it down.
lines.delivery: low, warm; her own ruined voice

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined

lines.delivery: low, warm; her own ruined voice

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: The reed orchards used to sing in a west wind. Whole hillsides of them. You would have liked it.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined

lines.speaker: p92_ysolde

lines.speaker: p92_ysolde
lines.text: The one ahead owns their shadow and lends it. Step out of somebody's shade without a word and you have insulted them. Give your shade to a stranger and you have done the finest thing you can do here.

lines.speaker: p92_ysolde

lines.speaker: p92_ysolde

lines.speaker: p94_bardo

lines.speaker: p94_bardo
lines.text: Low-pitched, loud-footed, lamp-blind son of a slack link. Speak in the Narrow, or go up and shout at the Bleach.

lines.speaker: p94_bardo
lines.text: Nineteen men, to jerking tethers. I cut each one in the housing, where I have to look at it. I do not say their names in here. The chains know them.

lines.speaker: p94_bardo
lines.text: The nine come down out of the sky to the rim, through the rings, and on down through the frame to the keel. The city's bones. Since the light took the rim we cannot get at them from on top, so we keep them from underneath.

lines.speaker: p94_bardo
lines.text: The city sways, and the bones take it one after another, never two together. Count the row. When the seventh speaks, be standing on a pin. A link under a speaking chain will throw a man, and it does not care which.

lines.speaker: p94_bardo
lines.text: The seventh's goods-cage. I pinned it up top myself, after the nineteenth, and may whoever knocks that pin out come back as a link on the wet side.

lines.speaker: p94_bardo
lines.text: Below the weights, in the keel, where the nine are made fast. The old capstan. Nobody has worked it since before my time, and it turns. I have nineteen strokes up here, and I have stood at the top of that stair and heard nineteen men hauling. I do not go down.

lines.speaker: p95_perpetua
lines.text: Light keep you true. Mind the hems, they are clean.

lines.speaker: p95_perpetua
lines.text: Seven years I have had nobody to robe. Stand still and let me see the length of you.

lines.speaker: p95_perpetua
lines.text: You cast, I will say that for you. Do not drip on the linen.

lines.speaker: p95_perpetua
lines.text: Four hundred. I wash every one each spring and hang it back on its peg, and nobody has put one on since the Fracture but the choir. In the old days the whole city went out at dawn in these. You walked out over the gulf with the Spire on your right hand, shining, and you sang.

lines.speaker: p95_perpetua
lines.text: A kilometre, almost level, and not a roof on it but the cage. The Tiers teach it to their children as soon as they can walk: walk in the shade of the one ahead of you. If there is no one ahead of you, run.

lines.speaker: p95_perpetua
lines.text: Black silk on black poles. The Altar's people go out under them every day, the choir before dawn and the clerics after it to polish the Eye, like a procession of black mushrooms. Keep under one and the light goes on round you. Step out, and it begins.

lines.speaker: p95_perpetua
lines.text: Two upstairs, keeping the winch. They let choir and bearers out of the mouth and nobody else. They look at the robe. They have never once looked at a face. Past the cage it is the Brother-Captain's half, Aurel Sant's. His men walk it in their own fire: the white parts round glass-fire.

lines.speaker: p95_perpetua
lines.text: The white never goes out. But when the sun is up there are two lights on the chain, and the two together are more than anything can stand in. Go by night. Go at the dead hour if you can: it lies thinnest then.

lines.speaker: p95_perpetua
lines.text: Bronze, forty feet across, at the back of the Altar. The only mirror in the Heights that is not a crime. It has gone white like everything, all but the middle, where they polish it every day with oil and ash. I have not seen it in seven years. I can tell you exactly what it looks like.

lines.speaker: p95_warden
lines.text: Light keep you true.

lines.speaker: p95_warden
lines.text: State your office.

lines.speaker: p95_warden
lines.text: Low-pitched. Speak up, or go back down the hole you came out of.

lines.speaker: p95_warden
lines.text: Choir and bearers. Nobody else has walked the chain since the Fracture, and nobody else will while this winch is kept.

lines.speaker: p95_warden
lines.text: Brother-Captain Sant has the far end, and the steps. His fire has not dipped in seven years. Ask him what yours is doing.

lines.speaker: p95_warden
lines.text: There is one note. The second note is sin.

lines.speaker: p96c_cantor
lines.text: Light keep you true.

lines.speaker: p96c_cantor
lines.text: Light keep you true. Sit, if you like, and keep the note company.

lines.speaker: p96c_cantor
lines.text: Light keep you true. In this room we speak softly, and we listen.

lines.speaker: p96c_cantor
lines.text: Every soul holds one true note. Sin is the note going flat. Grace is the note held.

lines.speaker: p96c_cantor
lines.text: The Church teaches that the second note is sin.

lines.speaker: p96c_cantor
lines.text: We taught under the east window, before. We teach here now.

lines.speaker: p96c_treble
lines.text: Light keep you true.

lines.speaker: p96c_treble
lines.text: Light keep you true. Speak low, please. I am practising.

lines.speaker: p96c_treble
lines.text: You are very loud. Out there they would call that low-pitched.

lines.speaker: p96c_treble
lines.text: I am holding it. The Cantor says if I hold it every night it will hold itself.

lines.speaker: p96c_treble
lines.text: We may sing here. Out there nobody speaks above the Narrow.

lines.speaker: p96v_albinus
lines.text: Light keep you true. You came up a long way to see snow.

lines.speaker: p96v_albinus
lines.text: You are loud for a mountain. Light keep you true, all the same.

lines.speaker: p96v_albinus
lines.text: She was here before any of us. She does not sleep much, and she will not be thanked.

lines.speaker: p96v_albinus
lines.text: Twelve of us. There were more once. Nobody comes up the mountain to join now.

lines.speaker: p96v_clemence
lines.text: Light keep you true. Speak softly. The Abbess is resting.

lines.speaker: p96v_clemence
lines.text: You are loud for a mountain. Light keep you true, all the same.

lines.speaker: p96v_clemence
lines.text: Twelve of us. There were more once. Nobody comes up the mountain to join now.

lines.speaker: p96v_clemence
lines.text: It does not go off the peaks, not even at the end of summer. We melt it for water.

lines.speaker: p96v_coriel
lines.text: Light keep you true. Sit, if you like. There is only the cot.

lines.speaker: p96v_coriel
lines.text: Light keep you true. Come in, and shut the door. The cold gets into everything.

lines.speaker: p96v_coriel
lines.text: Light keep you true, all the same.

lines.speaker: p96v_coriel
lines.text: Coriel. I am the Abbess of this house. There are twelve of us left. I am the oldest.

lines.speaker: p96v_coriel
lines.text: I watched it. From the tower you can see the Spire, on a clear morning. Three hundred sunrises I stood up there and watched, and I did nothing. That is all there is to say about it.

lines.speaker: p96v_coriel
lines.text: We ring it at dusk. It is the only thing that works.

lines.speaker: p96v_coriel
lines.text: Something comes up the cliffs every night, out of the dark below. The bell holds it while it rings. If you go down by the postern, be up before the last stroke.

lines.speaker: p96v_domitia
lines.text: Light keep you true. Are you hurt? Then go to the Abbess, not to me.

lines.speaker: p96v_domitia
lines.text: You are loud for a mountain. Light keep you true, all the same.

lines.speaker: p96v_domitia
lines.text: I keep the infirmary. Chilblains, mostly, and the old cough. Up here the cold is the only enemy you can see.

lines.speaker: p96v_domitia
lines.text: She gives away what she needs. I scold her for it, and she does it again the next day.

lines.speaker: p96v_fabian
lines.text: Light keep you true. Mind the ice on the step.

lines.speaker: p96v_fabian
lines.text: You are loud for a mountain. Light keep you true, all the same.

lines.speaker: p96v_fabian
lines.text: Ring the bell on the post and somebody comes. Most of the winter nobody rings it at all.

lines.speaker: p96v_fabian
lines.text: We do not get many. A ship on the shelf is a thing we talk about for a month.

lines.speaker: p96v_galen
lines.text: Light keep you true. Watch the sky. It changes fast up here.

lines.speaker: p96v_galen
lines.text: You are loud for a mountain. Light keep you true, all the same.

lines.speaker: p96v_galen
lines.text: She was here before any of us. She does not sleep much, and she will not be thanked.

lines.speaker: p96v_honoria
lines.text: Light keep you true. Walk on the flags. The garth is deep.

lines.speaker: p96v_honoria
lines.text: You are loud for a mountain. Light keep you true, all the same.

lines.speaker: p96v_honoria
lines.text: On a clear morning you can see it from the tower, a white needle a long way off. You can see the crack in it. We do not look at it much.

lines.speaker: p96v_liviana
lines.text: Light keep you true. Do not lean on the parapet.

lines.speaker: p96v_liviana
lines.text: You are loud for a mountain. Light keep you true, all the same.

lines.speaker: p96v_liviana
lines.text: She was here before any of us. She does not sleep much, and she will not be thanked.

lines.speaker: p96v_marcellin
lines.text: Light keep you true. We are not used to new faces.

lines.speaker: p96v_marcellin
lines.text: You are loud for a mountain. Light keep you true, all the same.

lines.speaker: p96v_marcellin
lines.text: Sister Ottavia rings it at dusk. Whatever comes up the cliffs stops while it rings.

lines.speaker: p96v_marcellin
lines.text: On a clear morning you can see it from the tower, a white needle a long way off. You can see the crack in it. We do not look at it much.

lines.speaker: p96v_ottavia
lines.text: Light keep you true. Do not touch the rope.

lines.speaker: p96v_ottavia
lines.text: You are loud for a mountain. Light keep you true, all the same.

lines.speaker: p96v_ottavia
lines.text: Twelve strokes at dusk. While it rings, whatever comes up the cliffs lets go of the rock. When it stops, it does not.

lines.speaker: p96v_ottavia
lines.text: It is mine to ring. My hands know the weight of it, and the bell knows my hands.

lines.speaker: p96v_prisca
lines.text: Light keep you true. Shut the gate behind you, when you go.

lines.speaker: p96v_prisca
lines.text: You are loud for a mountain. Light keep you true, all the same.

lines.speaker: p96v_prisca
lines.text: She was here before any of us. She does not sleep much, and she will not be thanked.

lines.speaker: p96v_quintin
lines.text: Light keep you true. The wind is from the south today.

lines.speaker: p96v_quintin
lines.text: You are loud for a mountain. Light keep you true, all the same.

lines.speaker: p96v_quintin
lines.text: On a clear morning you can see it from the tower, a white needle a long way off. You can see the crack in it. We do not look at it much.

lines.speaker: p96v_quintin
lines.text: She was here before any of us. She does not sleep much, and she will not be thanked.

lines.speaker: p97_scav
lines.text: Light keep you true. You are a long way up for a stranger.

lines.speaker: p97_scav
lines.text: Light keep you true. Mind the line. It does not look like anything.

lines.speaker: p97_scav
lines.text: Speak low or go down.

lines.speaker: p97_scav
lines.text: There, where the dark stops. Things left on it are not ours and not yours. Past it you go from shadow to shadow and you do not dawdle between.

lines.speaker: p97_scav
lines.text: He goes up every night, further than any of us, to the old market. He counts the ones who are still standing in it. Ask him why. He will tell you somebody should.

lines.speaker: p97_scav
lines.text: Go at night. The dead hour if you can wait for it. Wrap your face and glove your hands. And keep quiet on the third tier: that street belongs to the choir.

lines.speaker: p97_scav
lines.text: There is a ring in the wall at the east end of the shelf. The line that goes on it is up in the garden, coiled on the parapet. Whoever gets up there by the streets can let it down, and after that it is one climb.

lines.speaker: p97_tallyman
lines.text: Light keep you true. Keep your voice where mine is.

lines.speaker: p97_tallyman
lines.text: Light keep you true. Low. They are two streets down.

lines.speaker: p97_tallyman
lines.text: Low. Or go and be loud somewhere I am not.

lines.speaker: p97_tallyman
lines.text: Every night. I stand here and I count them, and I cut it on the pole, and I chalk it on the pillar. Fourteen. Thirteen. A long while at thirteen. Nine tonight. Nobody comes for them. They are only less, a little at a time, the way a gull goes in that light.

lines.speaker: p97_tallyman
lines.text: It was a market on the morning it happened. You can see what they were doing. One was taking a coin. I do not know their names. I used to make names for them, and I stopped.

lines.speaker: p97_tallyman
lines.text: They do not hear words. They hear noise. Run, and they hear you. Strike something, and they hear you. Sing, and they will come up a house to find the mouth it came out of. Walk, and keep your voice in your chest, and you are a wall to them.

lines.speaker: p97_tallyman
lines.text: Shadow to shadow, the way you cross a river on stones. Every shadow up here lies north. The dead hour is the kindest. By day I would not put my hand out of that arcade.

lines.speaker: p97_tallyman
lines.text: The street is shut above the market. I have not looked for a way round. Things live on the chains. I leave them be, and they leave the count be.

lines.speaker: p9_ada
lines.text: Good day to you. Softly. I sit out here more, now, under it. It does not sound, but I like to be under it.

lines.speaker: p9_ada
lines.text: Does it ring? True enough, I suppose. Keep it low.

lines.speaker: p9_ada
lines.text: I have buried a husband and I have hung his reed twice. I will not be shouted at on my own step.

lines.speaker: p9_ada
lines.text: Seventy years in one street. It was louder when I was a girl. Everything was.

lines.speaker: p9_ada
lines.text: Joram went in 418. The family holds the note until the body lets go, and in the old days it was sung out after. It cannot be now. The Hedge eats a note before it is halfway to the door.

lines.speaker: p9_tomas
lines.text: Does it ring? True enough. The wagon is loaded, and it hums, and I find I am used to it.

lines.speaker: p9_tomas
lines.text: The wagons do not creak any more. They hum. You feel it through the seat. A man could miss a creak.

lines.speaker: p9_tomas
lines.text: I have one good hand and a bad temper. Choose which you want to speak to.

lines.speaker: p9_tomas
lines.text: Timber comes out of the clearing and goes into the town, and the Hedge takes the noise off it at the gate. I have wondered where the noise goes.

lines.speaker: p9_tomas
lines.text: The Synod counts timber by the load. It does not count what the load weighs on a man.

lines.speaker: pim
lines.text: Something whistled my whistle from the culvert. Only me and Lyra know my whistle. I didn't go. I nearly went.

lines.speaker: quist
lines.text: We do not harvest, whatever the pamphlets in the Reach say. We relieve. A man walks out of the Greening with his whole life on his back and nowhere to put it down. We take it from him. Most of them look relieved at six seconds.

lines.speaker: quist
lines.text: Seventy-four thousand, and not one of them filed. The Hush did that, not us. We are the only people who ever came back to write them down.

lines.speaker: quist
lines.text: Sable. I taught her to rule a page. Ruler, nib, blotter; she had the straightest hand I ever saw. She designed the harvest schedule herself, you know. I only signed it.

lines.speaker: rooke
lines.text: The Synod sends the saws. I hold them. Somebody has to hold them who will stop when the patient asks. The Inquisitor has asked for my list of sap-marks. I have been slow to find it.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Entry: the Deep Woods. One wreck, twenty-six souls, a press, and me.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: A courier-cutter cannot carry anything heavier than paper and proctors. She was not carrying; she was listening, to four hundred and thirty-two cores murmuring in our hold. If there is anything under her hatch it is evidence: the Office seizes vox-bottles off the Rust Coast boats. If you open that hold, do not unstopper them in the dark. Quiets come through an open bottle like water through a sluice.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: I did not merely sign the catalogue. I designed the harvest schedule. I made it efficient. That is what I was good at.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Entry: the Hush does not take names. It takes the people and leaves the names lying about, like coats. The Catalogue only learned to pick them up.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: I have read his calibration records. Two percent survival at Stage Nine. He wrote that number himself, in a very steady hand, and then he went and lived outside a hedge.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: I hold the manifests for every core that captain has carried. Eleven consignments. I know the total. He does not want to. One day I will read it to him, one name at a time.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Stage Nine of the Vance Sequence. I filed it. The Cantor goes down in white because I wrote 'in white' on the form, so that she would not be mistaken for staff.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Entry: the subject asks the subject about the subject. Sable is a Veil designation. My own name is one of the three things I have left, and I do not spend it on strangers.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Crystallized song. A voice, bled out and set. I can read the name off a core the way you would read a label off a jar. That is what the Veil trained me for.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Two hundred and six Hollows in the Sunken Court. I read twenty names a night. Ten years and two hundred and twenty days to finish, and then you start again, because by then the first ones have stopped answering to them.

lines.speaker: tam
lines.text: My Essa. Forty years dead, near enough; the pox took her the year the old king went into the glass. She used to call me Tammy. Nobody else ever did, before or since. And now something out past the thorn calls me Tammy, three or four nights in the eight, and three nights ago it came up the Flume in her voice, singing The Miller's Daughter, which is ours. Mine and hers.

lines.speaker: tam
lines.text: Everyone says never answer it. I know what they say. I say she gets the second verse right, and the Hedge could not know the second verse.

lines.speaker: tobiah
lines.text: I learned the Vance Sequence at fourteen. I asked its author to sign my copy. He did. Then he looked at it for a long time and told me to keep the charts somewhere the Factor would not look.

lines.speaker: tobiah
lines.text: Three bolts of silk to close the hole and a relief valve to stop her bursting the patch the first time Vane gets clever. Then hops. Forty miles, down, cool the tank, forty miles. It'll be like crossing a river on stepping-stones, if the stones were on fire.

lines.speaker: umber
lines.text: Entry: a stranger, polite, at the wrong end of the continent. Sit. Not there. That is where the proctors will come from.

lines.speaker: umber
lines.text: I am a day-book, not a cure. Say what you came to say.

lines.speaker: umber
lines.text: Precision, please. I was trained to record everything, including the tone.

lines.speaker: umber
lines.text: I copied the harvest schedule fair, fourteen times, in a straight hand. Sable designed it. I only made it legible. That is what I was good at.

lines.speaker: umber
lines.text: Entry: the Hush does not take names. It takes the people and leaves the names lying about, like coats. The Catalogue only learned to pick them up.

lines.speaker: umber
lines.text: I have seen his calibration records; Sable kept them. Two percent survival at Stage Nine, in a very steady hand. He lives outside a hedge now, and I am told the hounds will not touch him.

lines.speaker: umber
lines.text: Eleven consignments to Whisper-Grove. The archivist there holds the manifests and knows the total. I copied the totals and did not add them up. One day she will read it to him, one name at a time.

lines.speaker: umber
lines.text: Stage Nine of the Vance Sequence. Sable filed it. I ruled the lines on the form. 'In white' is in her hand, so that the Cantor would not be mistaken for staff.

lines.speaker: umber
lines.text: Umber is a Veil designation, as Sable is. She is the last archivist of the Silent Veil, and she is in Whisper-Grove, reading names to the drowned, twenty a night. I was her junior. I could not stay and read with her, and I could not leave either, so I am here, which is neither.

lines.speaker: umber
lines.text: Crystallized song. A voice, bled out and set. I can read the name off a core the way you would read a label off a jar. That is what the Veil trained me for.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Bought with money I'd rather not discuss, from people I'd rather not name. She holds eighteen if nobody's fat and she lifts with three tanks.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: I carry one. Labelled with a name I won't say. Almost certainly a fake. I have never unstopped it, and I think about it every night.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Twelve crates of replacement cores for the quarry garrison. I don't ask what's in them. I have been very carefully not asking for two years. It is a skill.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: She'll fly. Forty-mile hops, if Tobiah can close the tank and stop the seam weeping. Further than that, she needs a whole new lift-tank, and there's only one coast that sells them without asking whose ship it is.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: She went down east of here with the willow-crown in her bow. Her listening-horn will still be working; those things outlive their crews. It was our hold she was listening to. Four hundred and thirty-two, murmuring. We're a bell. I've been ringing it for two years.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: North. Big marble thing in a ring of graves. The Cantor wants to go there. I'm not going to be the man who tells the Cantor no.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Twenty-one souls, a hold that murmurs, and a lift-tank with a weep in the seam. She'll get us off this water. Further than that I won't promise anybody.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: One thousand three hundred and forty-two. I know the number now. I didn't want to; somebody made me hear it. The Office has me in a file under "reliable, does not ask questions." I am asking questions now. Loudly.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: I've flown over it twice with cargo. Never put down. You don't, here. The Hollows walk out across the water toward the ladder like they've been waiting for a ship, and then they walk back.

lines.speaker: vosk
lines.text: Stage Nine. Source: Cantor, local, one. Collar: standard. Wire: standard. It is a procedure, not a sacrifice. The Church likes the robes; we like the yield.

lines.speaker: vosk
lines.text: A resource. It will yield without limit if correctly relieved. That is the Arbiterium's phrasing, not mine, and I confess I do not entirely follow it.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: Hello, hello.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: They don't talk. Mam said that's holy. Mam said if I sang nice the Quiet would come and be kind to me. It wasn't going to be kind, was it.
lines.match: They don't talk. Mam said that's holy. Mam said if I sang nice the Quiet would come and be kind to me.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: She's teaching me the skipping one. Too loud brings the hounds, too still brings the Hush. You have to be in the middle. That's called the Narrow.
lines.match: She's teaching me the skipping one. Too loud brings the hounds, too still brings the Hush.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: Orchard town. Used to be. Now it's a town inside a hedge that eats its own noise.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: Capital of the Resonant Reach, under the seal of a queen who has been dead a hundred and forty years. Since 417 the Consortium has milked the Growth Anchor's root from the quarry, and the law is going soft. Saplings split cobbles overnight.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: Three men deep of thorn and packed wool. It swallows our sounds so the hounds don't hear. Don't go near it after dark.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: Planted in 417 after the first hounds came. It keeps the Narrow for us. But at the dead hour it has started to speak, in the voices of our dead. Never answer it. Answering tells it you are there.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: Too loud brings the hounds, too still brings the Hush. Every child knows the rhyme.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: Mortals live in the band between two predators. Speak in a murmur. Keep a hush-lamp lit so no room ever goes silent. In siphoned country a person who falls truly silent begins to unwrite: warmth first, then name, then outline.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: Static with teeth. They come to music. Hounds, mostly, round here.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: What song becomes when the Hush bites it. They hunt voices because every voice is a small song, and they wear what they eat. Aether-Glass breaks them; glass shot from an ordinary pistol will do. They will not cross the glassed.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: What's outside. The quiet. We don't talk about it, which I suppose is the point.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: It is not empty. It is a silence that is alive, patient, and hungry, and it does not kill what it takes. It digests. Where a law thins, the Hush leans in. The Tongueless worship it as the Merciful Quiet. They are right that it is quiet.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: What's under the quarry. The Consortium drills it. Pays the town's bread, the Governor says.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: The Root of the Growth Anchor, 174 Hz. The Spire is the tower you can see; the Anchor is what is inside it, and the Root is where it drinks. There is something singing down there, a lullaby, and it keeps losing the tune.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: One Note, One Law, One Hand. They took our bells for bore-teeth.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: Five organs that need each other and hate each other: the Glass Court of dead kings, the Choir-Church, the Arbiterium, the Consortium of Bores and the Office of the Catalogue. And the Carillon Legions, every one of them running on a stolen name.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: The green river. Aqueduct, really, from the Anchor country. You can drink it if you boil it twice. Old Tam sits at the crossing of a night and listens to it.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: The Chlorophyll Flume carries Growth-water down from the Anchor's country to the orchards. It has been running sweeter and faster since 417, which is not good news. What it carries, it also carries voices in.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: The Choir-Church. They took the bells in 417, for the bore's teeth. They are coming back up the road to sing over us, and that is supposed to be a blessing.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: The Choir-Church of the Pure Note holds that the Light let go because one voice shouted at the Dawning Spire. Its Flambeau burn what sings off-key. Ignatius Crane leads the column coming to Oakhaven; his left hand was bleached white at the Dawning.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: The Church is coming to hold the Pure Note over the town. On Hearthday. They say it is a blessing.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: A four-hour unison hold at 174 Hz, sung at the casing with a collar and a wire. The Vance Sequence, Revision Seven, Stage Nine. Source: Cantor, local. They did the same thing at the Dawning Spire in 412 and the Light let go.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: The Governor's son. Lives outside the Hedge in a charcoal-burner's hut. The hounds won't touch him. People say that tells you something.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: Chief Resonant Engineer of the Consortium by twenty-seven. He calibrated the bore at the Dawning Spire. His left arm is Light-glass, Stage Three and spreading; anyone who knows glass can read his past off his skin.

lines.speaker: aegis

lines.speaker: shared_af_aoede

lines.speaker: shared_af_aoede

lines.speaker: shared_af_aoede
lines.text: I couldn't say. But I'll tell you what I heard: The Factor keeps Consortium brigandine and a steam-maul in Greenhall. At Consortium prices, naturally.

lines.speaker: shared_af_aoede

lines.speaker: shared_af_aoede

lines.speaker: shared_af_aoede

lines.speaker: shared_af_aoede

lines.speaker: shared_af_aoede

lines.speaker: shared_af_aoede

lines.speaker: shared_af_aoede
lines.text: I couldn't say. But I'll tell you what I heard: Davin Hale sang his mother's harvest song at the Boar. The hounds sang it back. That was the last anyone saw of Davin.

lines.speaker: shared_af_aoede

lines.speaker: shared_af_aoede
lines.text: I couldn't say. But I'll tell you what I heard: Keep your voice in your chest. Keep your lamp lit. Do not go to the Hedge at the dead hour, whatever it says, whoever it sounds like.

lines.speaker: shared_af_aoede
lines.text: I couldn't say. But I'll tell you what I heard: Tam the night-hummer listens to his dead wife at the Flume crossing. We all know. None of us has the heart to tell him what she is.

lines.speaker: shared_af_aoede
lines.text: I couldn't say. But I'll tell you what I heard: Bettany at the market stall takes coin for tonic but she would rather take eggs. Nobody has eggs. The hens went quiet first.

lines.speaker: shared_af_aoede
lines.text: I couldn't say. But I'll tell you what I heard: The Fenning twins went down the culvert after their dog on Driftday last. Abner Fenning still sets a lamp in their window. He keeps the culvert key on a nail.

lines.speaker: shared_af_aoede
lines.text: I couldn't say. But I'll tell you what I heard: The Cantor sang the Tanner boys into the ground side by side, after the bore head went on the platform. Marten and Old Coyle with them. She has not been the same since.

lines.speaker: shared_af_aoede
lines.text: I couldn't say. But I'll tell you what I heard: Nell Carder has not let the boy out of the mill since the Grafters posted the inspection. She says he has a cough. It is not a cough.

lines.speaker: shared_af_aoede
lines.text: I couldn't say. But I'll tell you what I heard: Red was redder when I was a girl. Summers were warmer. Everyone over thirty says so. The young ones think we are mad.

lines.speaker: shared_af_aoede
lines.text: I couldn't say. But I'll tell you what I heard: The dead are buried with bound jaws and a stone on the tongue so they cannot ring. We have not rung a bell in this town since the Synod took them.

lines.speaker: shared_af_nova
lines.text: Orchard town. Used to be. Now it's a town inside a hedge that eats its own noise.

lines.speaker: shared_af_nova
lines.text: Our Cantor. Sings the births and the burials. Her father was taken in 417.

lines.speaker: shared_af_nova

lines.speaker: shared_af_nova

lines.text: Synod surgeons. They come for the burl-sick with saws.

lines.speaker: shared_af_nova
lines.text: The Church's burners. They carry glass-fire the hounds will not cross.

harrow.name: Old Harrow, gate-warden
harrow.who: Old gate-warden of Oakhaven; dry, gruff, low-voiced; shuts the gate after dusk and puts shouters out through the thorn.

lyra.name: Lyra Ashgrove, Cantor of Oakhaven
lyra.who: Cantor of Oakhaven, Tobin Ashgrove's daughter; a trained, clear, warm voice with a fierce moral spine; voiced only before Whisper-Grove.

lyra_ruined.name: Lyra Ashgrove, her own ruined voice
lyra_ruined.who: Lyra after she lost her voice; speaks again only once Kaelen has told her everything (flags.lyra_voice): low, breath-heavy and cracked, a Cantor's diction and warmth still under it.

kaelen.name: Kaelen Vance, the Dissonant Blade
kaelen.who: Governor's son and former Chief Resonant Engineer for the Synod; glass left arm from the Foundry; lives outside the Hedge; weary, understated, low gravel, dry; wants to carry all of it alone.

hetty.name: Hetty Bram of the Boar & Dulcimer
hetty.who: Landlady of Oakhaven's tavern; brisk, dry, hard-eyed; has put out bigger men than you; no singing in her house since Davin.

vane.name: Captain Vane of the Drift-Kestrel
vane.who: Corsair captain of the airship Drift-Kestrel, retired from the sea on account of the sea; gallows humour and bravado over old grief (in 414 he held the axe ten heartbeats before he cut the hawser, forty-eight men); mid-age, big voice, often tired.

rooke.name: Surgeon-Grafter Anselm Rooke
rooke.who: Surgeon who has cut more limbs than any butcher in the Reach and done every one with care; clipped, precise, clinical, grim; knows the sap-mark and the Inquisitor's list.

orla.name: Orla Hale
orla.who: A woman turning to wood, rooted to her floor; gentle, dry and wry; asks about Davin.

pim.name: Pim Carder
pim.who: A small boy with something wrong with his hands; whispers; told by his Mam not to talk about it.

vosk.name: Factor Adela Vosk, Consortium of Bores
vosk.who: Consortium factor in lenses that show pitch as colour; cool, precise, mercantile; keeps Legionnaires, counts voices as replaceable.

aldric.name: Governor Aldric Vance
aldric.who: Governor of Oakhaven and Kaelen's father; harried, ironic, an older official pressed between the Factor and the Church; sold the Root to feed the town.

tobiah.name: Tobiah Marsh, engineer
tobiah.who: Junior Engineer on the Oakhaven night shift, later second engineer of the Drift-Kestrel; anxious, fussy, dry despair about engines; younger man's voice.

bettany.name: Bettany, midwife and tonic-maker
bettany.who: Oakhaven midwife and tonic seller; warm, motherly, brisk, prices in coppers; has hummed half the town into the world.

tam.name: Old Tam, the night-hummer
tam.who: Old night-hummer who listens at the water for a singer who comes at night; slow, quiet, murmuring.

hob.name: Hob Wendle, tanner
hob.who: Tanner whose trade has died; gruff, heavy, grieving; has buried two apprentices this year.

nell.name: Nell Carder
nell.who: Keeper of a shut mill, very likely Pim's Mam (shared surname); guarded, protective, sharp; has a sick man in the house with a cough.

ignatius.name: Ignatius Crane, Flambeau of the Pure Note
ignatius.who: Flambeau of the Choir-Church; tired, severe, formal, a man of long calm who has burned men for less.

townsman.name: Oakhaven orchardman
townsman.who: Ordinary Oakhaven orchardman; short, wary, murmuring.

townswoman.name: Oakhaven goodwife
townswoman.who: Ordinary Oakhaven goodwife; devout, hushing, protective of the children.

sable.name: Sable, Archivist of the Veil
sable.who: Archivist of the Silent Veil who keeps the Bound Ledger; soft, rhythmic, haunted, exact; speaks in "Entry:" form.

halder.name: Halder Wick
halder.who: A Hollow in drowned Whisper-Grove, repeating the loop of laying a table for a family; breathy fragments.

quist.name: Registrar-General Quist
quist.who: Registrar-General of the Office in the drowned city; mild, courteous, bureaucratic menace (hot water, clean chair); Mallow is on loan from the Arbiterium, he says.

aegis.name: The Aegis Sentinel
aegis.who: Nine feet of Catalogue bronze and bell-bronze with DEFEND THE SINGERS stencilled on the chest; speaks in slow capitals over a chord; a boy of the Cloister choir, WG-41,005, is inside it.

lamplighter.name: The lamplighter
lamplighter.who: A Hollow with a one-line loop; breathy, trailing.

bettis.name: A Hollow on the bench (Bettis Renn)
bettis.who: A Hollow on a bench asking for a name; breathy, trailing.

mags.name: Mags Tennant, first mate
mags.who: First mate of the Kestrel; lost her hearing, reads lips, signs hand-cant; blunt, dry; arm in a sling in the Deep Woods.

sexton.name: Amos Fell, the Hollow sexton
sexton.who: A Hollow gravedigger in the Spectral Woods, digging the same grave over and over; old, low, trailing.

mourner.name: A Hollow mourner
mourner.who: A Hollow woman with lilies, always late for a funeral; breathy, trailing.

wren.name: Wren
wren.who: A girl of about eight, left singing in a ring of hush-lamps by the Quiet Faith; sings too loudly, whispers when she remembers.

weaver.name: The Phantom Weaver
weaver.who: A named horror of the Cacophony that weaves forgotten voices into a shroud; speaks in whoever it ate (see voiceOf).

wearer.name: The Wearer
wearer.who: The Cacophony that wears Tobin Ashgrove and has practised the player's voice and everyone's; speaks in borrowed voices, warm and exact.

requiem.name: The Requiem
requiem.who: A Cacophony of three hundred years of funeral offices from the Mausoleum of Chords; a mourning veil, a broken bell for a head; sings in the dead's voices.

core_voice.name: The voice in the core
core_voice.who: The small human voice inside a cracked Office or Carillon core when the bell goes still: a named victim, saying their own name three times.

deacon.name: The Deacon of the Unrung Bell
deacon.who: Leader of the Quiet Faith brothers, tall, carries a clapperless bell; his mouth is bound in linen and he signs; kind, sure, low and devout. (Proposed barks voice him murmuring through linen; the game shows him signing.)

captain.name: Outrider-Captain Hal Brennick
captain.who: Officer of the Arbiter's column sent to find out why OC-742 stopped reporting; carries a lit hush-lantern and a sabre; Office dialect, unhurried, courteous, a competent man.

pressman.name: Pressman Mallow
pressman.who: Office of the Catalogue, Second Pressings, on loan from the Arbiterium; a hand-press on his back, a round-book on a chain; big, slow, flat, a clerk of forgetting.

proctor.name: Catalogue Proctor
proctor.who: Grey-oilcloth officer of the Office with a hand-press tuned to 741; flat Office dialect; never uses a verb with a person as its object.

legionnaire.name: Carillon Legionnaire
legionnaire.who: Soldier in a bell-shaped helm with a person's name murmuring inside; bell-throated, few words, liturgical cadence.

marine.name: Cutter-Man
marine.who: Office boarding crew in grey oilcloth with a grapnel line; reels people in; flat Office dialect, treats people as consignment.

bosun.name: Bosun Teller
bosun.who: Bosun of the Office cutter OC-742; keeps the hold key and the count of 432; very polite, exact (he counted crates on and off at Oakhaven for two years).

outrider.name: Office Outrider
outrider.who: Crossbowman of the Arbiter's column in grey oilskin; prefers forty feet to four; calm, distant, reporting.

tobin.name: Tobin Ashgrove
tobin.who: Cantor of Oakhaven, Lyra's father (taken in 417); warm, fatherly baritone; called her "lark".

lyra_child.name: Lyra at twelve
lyra_child.who: Lyra's voice as a girl of twelve, singing the calling-song.

cantor_old.name: A Cantor three hundred years dead
cantor_old.who: An old Cantor of Memory from the Mausoleum of Chords; solemn, ancient, sung.

chorus_mourners.name: A chorus of mourners
chorus_mourners.who: A hundred voices, all mourners, from the funeral offices of the Mausoleum.

chorus_congregation.name: The Cloister congregation
chorus_congregation.who: Two hundred voices singing Hymn 9 slightly out of time (the Cloister of the Lost Choir).

player_mother.name: The player's mother (as the Weaver wears her)
player_mother.who: The player's mother, a warm calling voice; generic woman's voice in recording since it cannot be tailored.

player_kin.name: Someone the player knew (brother, first mate, or the buried)
player_kin.who: The hedge voice: the player's brother, a first mate they left in the water, or someone they buried, by player background. Record neutral and warm.

player.name: The player
player.who: The player's own voice as the Wearer plays it back; generic mid voice; cannot be cloned.

wg41005.name: WG-41,005, a boy of the Cloister choir
wg41005.who: The boy inside the Aegis; small, plain, saying his intake number.

sister.name: A Church sister
sister.who: One of the two kind women of the Church who keep Lyra in custody (ch. 9): grey with gold at the collar, gentle, believing.

aldric_tube.name: Governor Aldric Vance, down the speaking-tube
aldric_tube.who: Aldric heard four hundred feet up a brass tube (ch. 10): small and tinny, tired, level, counting.

pumpman.name: A man at the pumps
pumpman.who: A Hollow at the Root-vault pumps, given back his name for the length of a breath (Book One ch. 10; the eight left).

lyra_fortunate.name: Lyra Ashgrove, "I. Am. Fortunate."
lyra_fortunate.who: Lyra with the wire in her throat, saying the rubric's words flattened onto 174 (ch. 10).

davin.name: Davin Hale
davin.who: Orla Hale's grandson, who sang the harvest home and could never hold the fourth line; heard only in the Hedge's mouth at the North Gate (ch. 11).

ada.name: Ada Pellow
ada.who: Mistress Pellow of Cooper's Row, fifty-one, who put new milk on Lyra's step every week; an ordinary, perfectly steady voice (ch. 11).

engineer.name: Pennick, the Kestrel's engineer
engineer.who: The Drift-Kestrel's engineer, Pennick, as Book One names him (ch. 8, 12, 21, 24): young, anxious, does the figures on a slate and does not like the answers.

tideweaver.name: The Tide-Weaver
tideweaver.who: Ilias Marren, who watches the threads and tells the Echoes (Book One, Echo I). Not the Phantom Weaver.
